principal_diagnosis: Paracetamol Overdose with early hepatotoxicity (ICD-10: T39.1X2A)
hospital_course: Patient was admitted for intentional paracetamol overdose. Paracetamol level was in the toxic range (180 mcg/ml) on admission with early hepatotoxicity (ALT 88, AST 102, INR 1.4). A 21-hour N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) IV protocol was initiated immediately. Liver function tests were monitored, with ALT peaking at 210 on day 2 before improving. INR normalized to 1.1 by day 3. Gastroenterology review found no signs of fulminant hepatic failure. Psychiatry liaison assessed the patient on day 1 and day 3. At discharge, the patient expressed remorse and denied current suicidal ideation. A family support plan was established. The psychiatry team recommended increasing her Sertraline dose to 100mg OD and arranged for continued outpatient care.

medication_changes.change: Dose increased from 50mg OD to 100mg OD
medication_changes.reason: Reviewed by psychiatry for management of Major Depressive Disorder.

allergies: No Known Drug Allergies (NKDA) - Verify with patient
follow_up: Urgent follow-up with Psychiatry OPD in 3 days. Repeat LFT in 1 week. Follow-up with Medicine OPD in 2 weeks. Patient and family have been counselled on safety planning and provided with a crisis helpline number. Instructed to return immediately for jaundice, severe abdominal pain, or any mental health crisis. Clinician signature required before discharge.
discharge_condition: Medically stable. LFT improving. Psychiatrically assessed as safe for discharge with plan.

flags.issue: Intentional overdose attempt requiring medical and psychiatric intervention.
Urgent psychiatric follow-up required in 3 days.
